To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: 
Subject: Warehouse-to-Store Transportation Plan — Balancing Cost and Carbon Under Practical Operating Rules

Context
Customer expectations, retailer scorecards, and our climate commitments require us to reduce logistics emissions without undermining service or inflating costs. Our warehouse-to-store network is evaluated on both delivered cost and carbon intensity. In practice, the lowest-price lanes tend to be more carbon intensive, while cleaner options can be more expensive or operationally restrictive. We need a clear, defensible plan that balances these competing goals while honoring day-to-day realities on the ground.

Operational Rules and Network Boundaries
Our plan must reflect how operations actually run:
- Route activation costs: Using a shipping route triggers a fixed setup charge tied to carrier contracting and handling readiness. A route is either active or inactive; if active, this charge applies regardless of volume.
- Minimum order quantities: Once a route is activated, we must move at least a defined volume over it to justify equipment and handling; partial loads are not accepted on these lanes.
- Supplier limits per store: To protect dock capacity, streamline vendor management, and maintain consistent delivery windows, each store can receive from no more than a set number of warehouses.
- Warehouse and store balances: Shipments cannot exceed available inventory at each warehouse, and every store’s minimum demand must be met.

Management Priority and Decision Framework
Leadership has established relative importance weights for cost and carbon. We will evaluate each candidate plan using a blended measure that:
- Applies the cost weight to total variable shipping spend across all active lanes,
- Applies the emission weight to total logistics emissions across those same lanes,
- Adds the full setup charges for any route we activate (these fixed charges are not scaled by the weights).
This approach keeps everyday spending and our carbon footprint visible in a single decision metric while preserving the true financial impact of route activation.

Goal
Develop a shipping plan that identifies:
- Which routes to activate,
- How many units to move on each active route,
while ensuring we do not exceed warehouse inventory, we satisfy every store’s demand, activated routes move at least the required minimum order, and each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses. The recommended plan will reflect the current cost and carbon weights and will make plain the trade-offs between cheaper but higher-emission routes and cleaner but more expensive options. We will also prepare sensitivity views so leadership can see how recommended routes change if the relative importance of cost versus carbon shifts.
